title: Introduce provision safety carveout and utilization telemetry sanitizer
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a configurable safety carveout that guarantees a small reserved headroom for critical tenants during aggressive decommits, plus a telemetry sanitizer to reduce false-positive utilization spikes in autoscaler signals.
description:
Motivation: In certain multi-tenant dedicated clusters aggressive decommits and ephemeral background noise in utilization sampling cause tenants with tight SLAs to see transient throughput drops and trigger unnecessary scale-ups or hard throttles. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) a provision safety carveout - a small, configurable per-pool reservation that is applied during scale-down windows to preserve minimal headroom for priority tenants; and 2) a utilization telemetry sanitizer - a processing stage that smooths and de-noises utilization signals before they feed the autoscaler and the Alerting/Telemetry pipeline.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a safety_carveout_percent to pool configs with an opt-in per-tenant override; implements a soft reservation allocator that deducts the carveout from decommitable capacity during scale decisions; introduces a streaming sanitizer that applies percentile-based spike rejection and exponential smoothing to per-tenant and per-pool utilization samples; updates dashboards and adds e2e tests and a canary rollout.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3124) [x] Unit + integration tests [x] E2E canary plan [x] Dashboard panels updated [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults

Related: ENG-3124 (design), ENG-3298 (telemetry cleanup), incident INT-4432 (Feb 2026 outage post-decommit), notes: this is opt-in by default (default carveout_percent=0) to avoid surprising existing tenants.

Implementation notes: The sanitizer runs as a pre-aggregator in the telemetry ingestion path and produces a sanitized_metrics stream consumed by autoscaler and the console. The soft reservation allocator is consulted during the decommit scoring pass and marks slots as "soft-protected" rather than fully reserved; these soft-protected slots can be reclaimed under emergency cluster pressure via admin override but are honored in automated graceful decommits and in warm-pool calculations.

review_comments: Alexei Morozov: Can we quantify expected cost impact for 1% / 2% carveout on a 1000 GPU fleet? Please add a short table or calculator in the design doc.

Priya Nair: Added a cost calc appendix to the design doc (docs/design/provision_safety_carveout.md) showing per-tenant reserved-GPU-hours and worst-case prepaid headroom. Impact for 1% on a 1000 GPU fleet ~10 GPUs reserved at steady state; included guidance for SRE to tune carveout_percent by pool.
Samira Khan: Telemetry sanitizer looks good but ensure we don't hide real microbursts that should trigger autoscale. Consider a tunable spike retention window and alert on sanitized vs raw deltas.

Priya Nair: Good point. Added spike_retention_ms and alert hooks to telemetry sanitizer config. Default retention is 250ms and we emit a delta metric raw_vs_sanitized_percent for auditing/dashboarding.
Diego Alvarez: Tests are comprehensive. Suggest adding a canary rollout config in helm chart to limit to 10% pools initially.
Priya Nair: Added helm canary flag and rollout notes under deploy_notes.
deploy_notes: Canary rollout: enable feature flag provisioning.safety_carveout for 10% of dedicated pools (helm values: safetyCarveout.canary.enabled=true safetyCarveout.canary.poolSelector=label:priority=low). Monitor metric telemetry.sanitizer.raw_vs_sanitized_percent and autoscaler.decommit_rejections for first 48h. If >1% of pools see unexpected RPM increases, revert flag. Full rollout: 72h after canary with progressive 25/50/100% rollout steps.
notes_on_backport: Backport target: release/2026.03 for clients using dedicated v2 autoscaler. No changes required to public API other than new optional pool config; migration SQL included. Backport will require re-running migration and ensuring the telemetry pre-aggregator is deployed before enabling carveout.
